newsitem.title: MEXICO: NorAm considering Mexico natgas supply--govt.
newsitem.headline: NorAm considering Mexico natgas supply--govt.

text.p: U.S. NorAm Energy Corp is considering bidding for natural gas distribution rights in the western Mexican state of Jalisco, a local government official said on Tuesday.

"During our working tour through Houston, NorAm directors said they are interested in the natural gas distribution project in the state and are considering participating," Jalisco Economic Promotion Minister Sergio Garcia de Alba told Reuters.
Garcia said the company could join with private Mexican construction firm Corporacion Gutsa in the bidding, and perhaps with another Canadian company.
NorAm and Gutsa unsuccessfully bid for natural gas distribution in the state of Chihuahua last month and the U.S. company has expressed interest in natural gas distribution in Mexico City.
Mexico is in the process of auctioning rights to natural gas distribution in different regions, in a move to encourage infrastructure development and use of the fuel.
The Jalisco concession would include the construction of a pipeline between the cities of Manzanillo and Guadalajara, and is expected to require an investment of about $300 million.
